The Most Dangerous Trade: How Short Sellers Uncover Fraud, Keep Markets Honest, and Make and Lose Billions — Richard Teitelbaum (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Profiles a dozen-plus famous short sellers (Chanos, Einhorn, Ackman and others): how they find targets, fund the position and survive the squeeze. It's the practitioner side of his short-research pages and his live ORCL short.

Off the Scales: The Inside Story of Ozempic and the Race to Cure Obesity — Aimee Donnellan (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: 2026 FT Business Book of the Year shortlist. Traces GLP-1 from early lab work to Novo Nordisk's rise and its fight with Lilly. It covers both his health/longevity interest and his Novo Nordisk research page.

The Infinity Machine: Demis Hassabis, DeepMind and the Quest for Superintelligence — Sebastian Mallaby (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: 2026 FT shortlist from a past winner (More Money Than God), based on 30+ hours with Hassabis. It's the human story behind his AI & Tech foundation-model pages.

John of John — Douglas Stuart (Literary Fiction)
Why Fred: Outside territory. A 2026 Booker shortlist novel from the Shuggie Bain winner. A young art graduate comes home to his strict Free Presbyterian father's croft on Harris; a quiet father-son family drama.

1929: Inside the Greatest Crash in Wall Street History — Andrew Ross Sorkin (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Narrative financial history of the 1929 crash built from never-before-seen Fed board minutes and private letters — same Lewis-style "you-are-there" journalism as The Big Short/Flash Boys, and lands squarely on his live AI-capex-bubble tracking (Djukanovic, Klement, Grantham).

Money Men: A Hot Startup, A Billion Dollar Fraud, A Fight for the Truth — Dan McCrum (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: FT journalist's 7-year investigation into the €20bn Wirecard fraud, told from the inside of the newsroom that broke it — same fraud-detective energy as Red Notice and his Hindenburg/Muddy Waters short-research pages.

Rise of the Machines: Drone Warfare in the Russia-Ukraine War — Illya Sekirin (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Insider account of how unmanned systems came to dominate the battlefield — direct match for his Fire Point Ukraine drone-manufacturing wiki entry and Rheinmetall defence thesis.

Angel Down — Daniel Kraus (Literary Fiction / Horror)
Why Fred: Outside territory — 2026 Pulitzer Prize winner — a squad of WWI soldiers find a fallen angel on the battlefield, told in a single unbroken sentence; a formally daring, genre-blurring novel with none of his usual finance/spy hooks.
